facts.text: Insurance intermediation represented 5% of Group revenue in 2025; Iute also reported fully digital MTPL in Albania and preparation of a subscription proposition combining travel, life and roadside assistance.
In 6M 2026, insurance brokerage revenue grew 59.6% year on year to 5.7% of total revenue; standalone motor and health products were targeted for later in 2026.
Iute Affinity publicly describes full-lifecycle administration, claims handling, partner coordination and multi-market standardisation as part of its role.

opportunities.name: Standalone motor
opportunities.note: Illustrative worked example. Not a roadmap recommendation.

Customer: Avoid legal, financial and mobility disruption
Current alternative and renewal behaviour to validate
Product: Core cover with an optional assistance layer
Limits, exclusions and proof of insurance must be legible
Trust bridge between digital policy and physical expectations
Business: Premium, commission and renewal are internal inputs
Model contribution after service, payment and exception costs
Test incremental adoption, not exposed-customer conversion alone
Partner: Carrier owns underwriting according to contract
Agree quote, bind, claims, data and escalation obligations
Assess portfolio sustainability, not only launch price
Operations: Policy changes, cancellation and refunds need named owners
Payment and issuance states must reconcile
A claim cannot expose the customer to partner complexity
Scale: Reuse orchestration, objects and event taxonomy
Localise carrier, wording, pricing, disclosures and claims
Extract shared capability only after pilot evidence

opportunities.name: Health + assistance
opportunities.note: Illustrative comparison. Requires deeper customer and privacy evidence.

Customer: Households seeking access and cost certainty
Need intensity may be high but benefit comprehension varies
Interview buyers, abandoners, users and cancellers
Product: Protection and service bundle must be evaluated separately
Waiting periods, networks and exclusions shape value
Validate whether annual or subscription framing is clearer
Business: Renewal value requires sustained perceived usefulness
Acquisition outside existing relationships may change the case
Partner: Carrier, assistance and medical networks may differ
Data boundaries and service SLAs are product constraints
Operations: Sensitive data requires purpose and access discipline
Service routing should feel like one front door
Scale: Coverage and provider networks vary materially
Shared policy wallet and service intake may still repeat
Local privacy and health regulation require validation

opportunities.name: Travel protection
opportunities.note: Illustrative comparison. Test event observability and frequency.

Customer: Traveller facing episodic financial and service risk
Purchase moment can be observable or explicitly declared
Validate frequency, trust and willingness to pay
Product: Territory, trip duration and exclusions must be clear
Service access may matter more than feature count
Business: Episodic purchase and annual cover have different economics
Model paid acquisition only if existing reach is insufficient
Renewal and cross-product value need evidence
Partner: Real-time policy and emergency-service availability matter
Assess claims data and incident escalation
Operations: Offline access to policy and help
Carrier outage cannot block emergency intake
Scale: Common journey with market-specific eligibility and wording
Use shared events and reconciliation controls

questions.question: Where is the largest constraint today: product breadth, penetration, renewal, standalone distribution or operating scale?

Where does Iute want stronger ownership across proposition, administration, servicing and claims? Where is carrier ownership the better choice?
Where do customer and operational failures concentrate today: quote, issue, payment, servicing, claims, reconciliation or data handoffs?
